rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Residential rental property owners may not use algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rents. Software providers and other coordinators may not use such software to facilitate agreements or coordinate pricing among competing residential landlords.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic rent-setting using competitors' nonpublic data
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental property owners in New Jersey, plus software providers and coordinators that operate algorithmic revenue management software or devices using nonpublic, competitively sensitive information from multiple owners to recommend rents, lease terms, or occupancy levels.
rules.exemptions: Does not prohibit spreadsheets requiring human analysis, publicly available rent estimation tools, traditional real estate listing databases, or government-administered affordable housing programs.
rules.penalty: The attorney general must set up a complaint portal for alleged violations. Existing remedies under the New Jersey Antitrust Act are preserved.
rules.quoted_span: The FAIR Act prohibits residential rental property owners from using algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rental prices.
rules.conflict_note: Taken from a secondary law-firm alert, not the statute text. The alert states an effective date of July 1, 2027, so the act is not yet effective as of 2026-10-01.
